clue.text: Pocket found in short jeans, perhaps

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its tail, so the final letter of the word comes off

parts.note: jeans are one example of this garment, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Someone finds a pocket on a pair of cut-off jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocket' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to trouser money is to pocket it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser is informal British slang for taking money and putting it away, often dishonestly, exactly as you would pocket it.

clue.text: Throw drug to incompetent fool

parts.note: to toss is to throw
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone flings narcotics at a bungling idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for a drunkard and is now British slang insult for a stupid, useless person.

clue.text: Expose falsehood Romeo gives one separate from the pack

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them
a lie is a falsehood
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Exposing Romeo's lie makes him an outcast from his friends.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlier is a data point or person lying well apart from the main group, far from the rest of the herd.

clue.text: Capture the sound of oceans

indicators.note: the setter wants the word as heard spoken, not as written on the page

parts.note: oceans are seas, and the plural sounds identical to the verb

explanation.surface: Someone tries to record the noise of the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize something is to grab it or take it by force, as an army would capture a town.

clue.text: Doctor and mother with part in performance

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig them
ma is an informal word for mother
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A physician and a mum both have roles in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performance' here is the British sense of a tiresome fuss, as in 'what a performance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tedious procedure or fuss, which British speakers also call a performance or palaver.

clue.text: One giving speech unsurpassed on island

parts.note: unsurpassed means the best
the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An orator talks on an island, giving the finest address there.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after; the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding the groom's chief attendant traditionally delivers a speech at the reception.

clue.text: Praise Britain? Not so much

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Britain
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether Britain deserves admiration, answered with 'not so much'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless God is to praise or glorify him, as in the hymn line bless the Lord.

clue.text: Dubious recycled plastic covering church

indicators.note: one part is wrapped around the other, enclosing it like a lid
recycled material is broken down and remade in new form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that the recycled plastic roof on a church is a good idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dubious about something means doubting it, which is what a sceptic, or skeptic, does.

clue.text: Bird gets one drink

parts.note: the martin is a swallow-like bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girlfriend, or a feathered bird, is bought a single drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail made with gin or vodka and vermouth, a classic alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Out of the running at this time and place

parts.note: now means at this time
'and' carries 'this' across, so this place means here

explanation.surface: A competitor is declared beaten, right here and now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nowhere' is used of a runner finishing unplaced, as in 'came nowhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or competitor that finishes nowhere is unplaced and has no chance at all of winning.

clue.text: Frame alien in fraud

indicators.note: one part sits inside the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick
ET, the extraterrestrial of Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: An alien is set up and framed in a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' tempts as a verb meaning to set someone up, but here it is the noun for a mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A setting is the mount or surround that holds a jewel or picture, just as a frame holds something.

clue.text: Stare at black line somewhere on face

parts.note: to eye something is to look hard at it
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a row is a line

explanation.surface: Someone stares at a black line drawn on a face.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch of hair above each eye is a feature located on the face, so the vague phrase fits.

clue.text: Spin doctor cagiest about ways to display costs

parts.note: PR is public relations, the trade of spin doctors

indicators.note: letters moved about are scattered and set down in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cagey publicist is evasive about how to present expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Labels attached to goods in shops are how a retailer shows each item's selling price.

clue.text: Starting to transform ceremony that's overused

indicators.note: the start of the next word is all that is wanted, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of transform
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to revamp a stale, tired ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trite has been said or done so often that it has lost its freshness and become hackneyed.

clue.text: Bath robe hides sign of increased blood flow

indicators.note: the two words together conceal the solution within their run of letters

parts.note: concealed across the two words

explanation.surface: A bathrobe conceals a flush of blood, perhaps after a hot bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulsing beat, as of a heart or a sore finger, comes as blood surges through the vessels.

clue.text: Struggle to get rid of dragon

parts.note: a battle is a struggle
to axe something is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: A fight to slay a dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a knight's quest, but 'dragon' is the informal word for a fierce, domineering woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon or battleaxe is a formidable, bossy, aggressive older woman in informal British usage.

clue.text: Complain I have shortened goal

parts.note: to object is to complain
the contraction I've, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone protests that their target has been reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective is an aim or target someone works towards, the same as a goal.

clue.text: Defended fair on condition uncovered rides dismantled

parts.note: just means fair

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken apart and can be reassembled differently

parts.note: if means on condition that

indicators.note: uncovering strips the outside away, leaving only the inner letters

parts.note: the inside of rides

explanation.surface: A fairground defended on condition that its rides were dismantled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be justified is to have been shown right or vindicated, so an action defended successfully.

clue.text: Sex with tenor among red hot ashes causes upsets

indicators.note: placed among something means set in the middle of it

parts.note: embers are glowing remains of a fire
it is a coy word for sex
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A tenor's fireside fling among the hot embers causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter someone is to make them resentful and aggrieved, which upsets them deeply.

clue.text: Kill former boyfriend with bit of envenomed sweet

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: only a small piece of the next word is used, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of envenomed
cute means sweet or endearing

explanation.surface: A murder plot against an ex-boyfriend using a poisoned sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute is to put to death, especially by legal sentence, which is to kill.

clue.text: Babies, regularly entertained by Oasis rivals, weep excessively

indicators.note: a guest entertained is held inside the host's home

parts.note: Blur were Oasis's great Britpop rivals in the 1990s

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Babies are entertained by a rival band and cry their eyes out.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis and Blur were rival British rock bands of the Britpop era.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to sob noisily and without restraint, which is to weep excessively.

clue.text: Joins golf course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: connects, as a verb
second meaning: a seaside course on sandy ground

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a member of a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means connects or couples things; the noun names a coastal golf course on dunes.

clue.text: More clamorous about one small charged particle returning

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the run is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the abbreviation for small
an ion is an electrically charged atom

explanation.surface: A physicist complains about a lone charged particle making a din as it returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamorous means loud and raucous, so more clamorous means louder, making more noise.

clue.text: Topless artistes gyrating for people in chairs

indicators.note: gyrating means spinning and twisting, so the letters whirl into new order
with its top removed, the word loses its first letter in a down clue

parts.note: taken as written, before its head is cut off

explanation.surface: Topless dancers gyrate for seated customers in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitters are people seated, such as models posing for a portrait, so people in chairs.

clue.text: Peer squeals endlessly, when excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and jumbled into a new order
without its ends the word keeps only its inner letters

parts.note: the inside of squeals

explanation.surface: A lord shrieks with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a nobleman or a verb for looking, but it is a person of the same standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is one's equal in age, rank or ability, as in a jury of one's peers.

clue.text: Cheeseparer to remove outside of stone

parts.note: to skin something is to remove its outer layer
flint is a hard stone

explanation.surface: A miser is so mean he would peel a stone to save something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the saying about a miser who would skin a flint.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeseparer is a stingy person who saves every scrap, the same as a miser.

clue.text: Brushed end of humerus and cried

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of humerus
wept means cried

explanation.surface: Someone grazed their funny bone and burst into tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep is to brush a floor clean, so swept is its past tense, brushed.

clue.text: Acts following foot faults

indicators.note: the word before this one comes after the word that follows it, so the order is swapped

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for foot
Acts of Parliament are laws

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire's calls follow foot faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaws are defects or imperfections in something, which are its faults.

clue.text: Offence shadow government engendered initially

parts.note: umbra is the dark core of a shadow

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words just before it

parts.note: opening letters of both words

explanation.surface: A shadow cabinet takes offence at what the government produced.
explanation.walkthrough: The umbra is the darkest part of a shadow, as in an eclipse.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, feeling slighted or resentful at something.

clue.text: Aiming to change European picture

indicators.note: changing the word means its letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An effort to alter the image of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, which is to imagine it.

clue.text: Serious attention given to bird's place

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
a bird's home is its nest

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher pays serious attention to a nesting site.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest person is sincere and intensely serious in manner or intention.

clue.text: Abandons wastelands

definitions.meaning: first meaning: leaves behind, as a verb
second meaning: barren, arid regions, as a plural noun

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means walks out on, as a soldier leaves a post; the noun names arid barren regions like the Sahara.
